title: What Though the Arm of Conquering Death
description: What Though the Arm of Conquering Death in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 599 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: What though th'arm of con-quer-ing death Does God's own house in-vade; What though our tea-cher and our friend Is num-bered with the dead;

lines: What though the arm of conquering death
What though our teacher and our friend
Though earthly shepherds dwell in dust,
The watchful eye in darkness closed,
Lord, be our Leader and our Guide,
And rule and keep our heart.
Yes, while the dear Redeemer lives,
And shall be fed with what he gives,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
